headline: A GRH Proof Enters the Review Queue
lede: Alessandro Masullo has circulated a proposed proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis ahead of schedule, inviting scrutiny rather than polished consensus. Early audits have already found problems; the mathematics now belongs to verification, formalization, and careful repair.

headline: An AI-Assisted Proof Faces the Dark
lede: Levent Alpöge’s enormous Lean formalization claims results reaching from the Riemann Hypothesis to its generalized forms. It compiles, but its statements, strategy, and mathematical meaning still require human examination in the quiet beyond the benchmark.

headline: Inkling 2 Mini Brings Reasoning Local
lede: Inkling 2 Mini is an open-weight 26.4-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 3.4 billion active parameters and looping layers for deeper reasoning. At roughly 20GB of memory, it targets coding, search, and tool use on consumer hardware.

headline: GPGME Fixes a Double-Free RCE Risk
lede: GPGME 2.3.1 patches a critical double-free flaw triggered by an unusually long OpenPGP user ID. Update shared libraries, refresh bundled desktop software, and rebuild statically linked applications before the stale pointer becomes an entry point.

headline: An IBM PC XT Runs an AI Coding Agent
lede: ClawDOS puts chat, file tools, compilation, screenshots, and memory onto a 4.77MHz-era machine with 640KB of RAM. The XT handles the agent interface; a modern computer quietly carries the TLS burden across the bridge.

headline: AI Coding Quietly Promotes Developers
lede: AI can generate implementation quickly, but someone still has to reject bad requirements, control data flows, and own the system’s trade-offs. The new burden is architectural whether or not the job title changes.
pullquote: Generated code does not eliminate architecture; it distributes the responsibility to everyone who approves it.

headline: Three Famous Problems Enter the Machine
lede: New AI-assisted Lean developments claim finite-time singularities for three-dimensional Euler and Navier–Stokes equations, alongside a proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis. The display number is only the beginning: matching formal statements to advertised mathematics remains the central test.

headline: Nine Inch Nails Live, Preserved at Scale
lede: NINLIVE gathers decades of setlists, tickets, photographs, recordings, and fan-contributed memorabilia into one searchable record. Its new streaming layer makes performances from 1988 through 2026 easier to hear—and harder to lose.

headline: Clojure Rewires the Programmer’s View
lede: Clojure makes code feel like data, state feel negotiable, and concurrency feel designed rather than improvised. Its lasting lesson is less about switching languages than learning to compose transformations with immutable structures and a live REPL.

headline: Insects Step Into the Portrait Studio
lede: Dara Ojo’s macro portraits make arthropods look curious, textured, and occasionally almost cuddly. Behind the charm is a field guide to pollination, decomposition, soil, pest control, and the small creatures holding ecosystems together.
